checks.item: 1. S6->S7 match cut (f380->f381) and S7 (f381-415): same tip, same place and direction, breaking out of the gill edge with a bubble puff, then rising out of the slit in a smooth arch
checks.evidence: Position holds. In full res the S6 tip at f380 is at about (567,997), and the top of the S7 tail at f381 is at about (575,994). On the phone sheet both sit at about the same spot in the tile (about x170, y325), so the cut reads as continuous. The bubble puff is there: two bubbles at f381, a cluster of 4-6 at f384-f397, gone by about f410. By f408-f415 the tail is a clean, smooth arch over the flank. What does not match is the shape and direction of the tip. At f380 it is a tapered, pointed dark-navy tip with a pale rim, travelling diagonally up-right at about 15-20 degrees. At f381 it is a lighter slate-blue piece with a dark outline, running straight up the slit and ending in a blunt, squared-off cap bent right and slightly down, like a bent pipe end. So the direction of travel changes from diagonal to vertical across the cut. From f381 to f404 the tail is a tight cane or inverted-J hook, not an arch. On the phone tiles f387-f402 it reads as a small '?'. The arch only shows from about f408. The tip pokes out over tan flank, not against open water.

checks.item: 2. S7->S8 cut (f415->f416) and S8 (f416-477): arch continues, no sharp L or V at the slit exit, no short stub at the cut, no dark-red wedge on the bend (f436-468)
checks.evidence: At the cut, f415 shows a tall arch rising well above the slit exit and reaching far right. f416 shows a much lower, flatter hook. The rise is about 70 px against about 120 px in f415, which is more than the about 0.83x camera change explains (eye about 145 px wide in f415, about 120 px in f416). The blue area of the eel drops from about 6,350 px to about 2,450 px across the cut. So a shorter stub replaces the arch. Through S8 the exit turns into a corner: a boomerang or V at f428, and a near right-angle 'Γ' at f436-f447. On the phone tiles f438-f447 it reads as a sharp '7'. Zoomed in, the bend has drawing glitches: an outlined rectangular box where the vertical and horizontal parts overlap (f440-f456); a stray thin line sticking up-left from the bend (f460); small brown rectangles (f460-f472); and dark-red triangle wedges sitting on the bend (f464, f468, f472). At f477 there is a diamond-shaped inner notch. On the phone tiles f459-f468 these show as a dark knot at the bend.

checks.item: 3. S9 (f479-538): smooth curve where the eel leaves the slit (no hard elbow, no inner notch, no dark facet); head reads as still INSIDE the opening, in shadow, eye just inside
checks.evidence: The outer corner is rounded, but the inner corner is a hard right-angle elbow in every S9 frame. At f479 the inner corner has a squared vertical step. At f486 and f500 it is a sharp pointed notch. At f520 and f536 an outlined dark pointed V wedge sits in the inner corner. On the phone tiles f489-f537 the eel reads as an inverted L ('Γ'). A faint diagonal seam (the gill-cover edge) also crosses the body at the bend (f479, f500, f520). The head is not in shadow. Only at f479-f486 is its lower end somewhat darker. From about f495 it is bright, lit silver-blue with a crisp outline, drawn in front of the dark-red slit with red showing to its right and below. The eye is large and white-ringed with a highlight, and clearly visible on the phone tiles (f492-f537). With the caption 'Its HEAD comes out LAST', a muted viewer sees the head already poking out of the slit, not hidden just inside it.

newProblems.claim: The eel's tail end swings in from the bottom-right edge, in front of the predator's pectoral fin. It shows up as a second thin blue eel, with no visible link to the body running off the top-right. On a phone it reads as a second eel or snake entering the shot just before the cut to S10.
newProblems.fix: Start the tail curl-in after the S10 cut. Or keep it off-frame in S9. Or frame S9 so the loop of body linking the two visible parts is on screen.

newProblems.claim: There is a squared step on the right outline of the tail where the outside arch meets the part lying in the slit (at about y 1140 full res). The outside part is slightly wider, with a flat bottom edge, so the arch looks pasted onto the in-slit body.
newProblems.fix: Taper or blend the outside segment into the in-slit segment so the outline stays continuous and the same width where the tail leaves the slit.

newProblems.claim: The tail end is a blunt, squared-off cap: a flat end with a corner, bent right and down. It is not the tapered, pointed eel tail seen in S6 and in the later arch. It also changes from dark navy with a pale rim (S6) to light slate-blue with a dark outline (S7) across the match cut.
newProblems.fix: Use the same tapered tail tip and a similar colour and rim treatment on both sides of the f380/f381 match cut.

checks.item: 1. S10 curl (f540-620): caught head and eye read at phone size at the slit; head vs thin raised tail stays clear
checks.evidence: Mostly fixed. At 1/3 (phone) scale the eye is a clear white-ringed dot of about 13-16 px (about 45 px full-res) at the slit in f540-543 and in every frame f553-620 I checked (f564-609 every 3rd). The head points down into the slit and the tapered tail rises separately as the '6', so the two ends read apart. The exception is f544-552: the thin tail tip slides up straight across the front of the caught head. The eye is half covered at f547 and f550-552 and fully hidden at f548-549 (only a white arc shows). For those 4-5 frames the tail tip also pokes above the head as a second prong at the slit. In f544-546 the tail tip is drawn as a frayed, fading 'broom' of 3-4 strands where it crosses the gill-cover edge, which shows as a small fan of strokes even at phone size. From f553 on the tail clears the head and everything reads cleanly.

checks.item: 2. S10 release (f612-640): eye stays visible while the head slides out, head comes free once around f628-630, about 10 frames on the freed head before the cut at f639
checks.evidence: Checked every frame f612-638. The eye is fully visible f612-619. From f620 to f626 the tan gill-cover edge crosses part of the eye: a crescent or ring at f621-623, a strip through the middle at f624-625, the lower part at f626. It is never fully hidden, and it is whole again from f627. Its size grows smoothly with no jump: about 44 px full-res at f612, about 50 at f626, about 56-60 at f629-631. The chin clears the cover at f629, the head is fully free at f630 and moves left without going back in, so it comes free once, under the 'gives one FINAL PULL' caption (f600-636). The freed head is on screen f630-638 (9 frames). Small caveat: the head drifts to the left edge, and at f638, the last frame before the cut, the frame edge cuts the eye in half, so there are about 8 clean frames.

checks.item: 3. S10 (f585-630): fin fringe along the raised tail is an even edge
checks.evidence: Checked f585, 588, 591, 597, 600, 603, 606, 609, 612, 615, 618, 621, 624, 627, 630 at 0.7-1.5x full-res. The fringe is an even band of constant width with fine hatched rays along both sides of the tail, all the way to a smooth rounded tip (f585, f591, f597, f603, f609). I saw no beads, lobes or segment joins, including where the tail passes behind the loop (f600, f606) and along the doubled strands above the loop (f618-633). It also stays even on the short raised stub at f636-637.

checks.item: 4. S10->S11 cut (f638->f639) and S11 (f639-735): clean cut, eel never lies across predator face or eye, swims away into clear water, no reed clump fades or ghosts
checks.evidence: The cut is a clean single-frame hard cut. Mean frame difference is 42-65 at f638->f639, against 6-12 for the frames on either side, and f639 shows no trace of f638. The eel's head touches the predator's lower cheek or throat under the gill line only in f639-641 (3 frames: overlapping at f639, on the jaw edge at f640, just touching at f641). It never reaches the eye. From f642 to f735 it stays clearly below and left of the predator. It swims to the lower left across open sand while the predator head moves up to the right edge and is cropped there (f699-729). Reed clumps and rocks enter from the left edge and scroll across with the pan (tall reeds f658-662; rock and sprig f680-702), staying fully opaque. I found no clump fading or ghosting in the middle of the frame. The reed wipe to S12 starts at about f731.

newProblems.claim: In the first beat after the cut the eel's tail is folded into a hard-cornered hairpin with a visible crease line at the fold: a V-fold at f639-641, an L-shape at f643, an acute fold at f645 and a hooked tip at f647. It looks like bent wire or a paperclip, not a flexing eel, and the sharp L is plain at phone size (f642-645).
newProblems.fix: Limit how much the S11 spine can bend per segment, or start the S11 pose from a smooth S or C curve, so the tail sweeps out of the S10 loop shape with no corner and no crease stroke.

newProblems.claim: As the tail tip slides up past the caught head, it is drawn frayed and soft-faded where it crosses the gill-cover edge, like 3-4 separate strands or a broom (f544-546). It then covers the eel's eye (fully at f548-549), so for about 0.15 s there are two prongs at the slit and no eye.
newProblems.fix: Route the tail tip around the head (outside or behind it) instead of across the front of the eye, and mask the tip against the cover with a hard edge instead of a feathered fade.

newProblems.claim: Where the eel's snout and neck cross the gill-cover edge as the head starts to slide out, the eel is faded with a soft brownish gradient instead of being cleanly hidden. At phone size this shows as a small pointed beak or hook on the snout (f617-619).
newProblems.fix: Use a hard occlusion mask at the cover edge (or a cover lip drawn on top) for these frames.

newProblems.claim: Large soft white bokeh discs (about 100 px full-res, about 30 px on phone) pop in for 1-2 frames and jump position. At f684 one sits right next to the eel, and at f708 one crosses the eel's body. They read as flickering smudges or ghosts, not drifting particles.
newProblems.fix: Slow the near-camera motes so each one drifts across over many frames, cap their size or opacity, or drop the biggest ones and keep them off the eel's path.

naive.q1:
SHOT-BY-SHOT, read from the pictures only (no captions):
S1 f000-f078: Side close-up of a brown fish's head. A blue-grey, glossy strap with a thin fin fringe comes out of the top of the red gill slit, hangs down across the orange pectoral fin and tapers to a point. It whips left at f006-f012, settles, and the camera pushes in slowly (f063-f078).
S2 f081-f114: Desaturated "earlier" shot. Extreme close-up of a gaping mouth with a grey strand hanging out that gets slurped in (f084-f090). The mouth shuts (f096) and the camera pulls back to the fish resting.
S3 f117-f171: Lab tank. A scanner bar sweeps over the fish and turns it into an X-ray. A glowing eel lies coiled in its belly: the head (with eye) points toward the fish's tail, and the thin tail rises toward the fish's head. Camera pushes in.
S4 f174-f267: Dissolve to a pink stomach. The blue eel is coiled with its head in the middle of the coil. The tail tip reaches a star-shaped pucker, enters it (f240-f246), the pucker opens (f249), the camera dives in, and the frame goes nearly black (f264-f267).
S5 f270-f309: Ribbed pink tunnel with a blue tapered spike pushing toward the vanishing point.
S6 f312-f378: Red comb-like arches with a bright crescent "window" to water and plants. The tip threads between the arches up to the window (flash at f375).
S7 f381-f414: Outside, tight on the fish's side. A tiny blue tip and a bubble appear at the top of the gill slit. The camera pulls back, the eye enters, and the tip grows and bends backward along the flank.
S8 f417-f477: Wide profile. A blue line grows rearward along the upper flank from the top of the slit.
S9 f479-f538: Close-up. A thick blue body lies along the flank. On the cut, a head with an eye is suddenly visible, tucked into the slit, and it does not move. The thin end slides in from the bottom right at f534.
S10 f539-f636: Tighter framing with lots of empty water. The body is a big loop over the fish. The thin end swings past the slit (f540-f546), then rises through the loop into a "6" shape. The head pops up and free of the slit at f627-f636.
S11 f639-f732: Wide seabed. The eel slips away from the fish's head toward the lower left; the fish stays put.
S12 f735-f741: A foreground plant wipes back to the S1 hook (loop point).

Q1, the tail in frame one: mostly yes. At f000 the strap's colour and texture (blue-grey, glossy, fin fringe) are clearly not the fish's own (brown and orange spotted), so it does not read as a fin. It tapers to a point with no head visible, and it moves on its own at f006-f012, so "the tail end of some long animal hanging out of the gill" comes across without words. What only the caption supplies is the word EEL (from pictures alone it could be a worm, a parasite or a sea snake) and the fact that the fish swallowed it.
Two picture problems:
(a) The tapering tip, which is the main cue that this is a tail, sits at roughly x 900-960, y 1550-1870 of 1920. That is inside the bottom ~20% where the Shorts title and channel row sit, and against the right-hand action-button column (also true at f009 and f030). On a real phone the "tail" cue is likely to be covered.
(b) This pose (out of the top of the slit, hanging down over the pectoral fin) never happens in the story. At f381-f477 the tail comes out of the top of the slit and lies backward along the upper flank.
Depends on caption: only for "eel" and "swallowed". "A tail, not a fin" holds up from the picture alone.
naive.q2:
Yes. This is the strongest part.
- f165 (X-ray): you can tell head from tail. The eye is on the right-pointing end; the thin tail curls up and to the left, toward the fish's head.
- f189-f231 (stomach): the same layout in colour. Head with eye in the centre of the coil, thin tail reaching up-left.
- f225-f246: the tail tip clearly hooks into the star-shaped pucker. You can see it is the tail (not the head) leaving, because the head with its eye stays visible in the coil until f252-f255.
- f249-f261: the pucker opens and the camera dives after the tail.
- f270-f309: the same blue tapered tip runs up the ribbed tunnel. Colour and taper keep the identity, so you don't lose the eel.
Small wobbles:
- f174-f186 (dissolve): a ghost X-ray eel at lower left (its head around (700,1440)) overlaps a coloured coil at the right edge whose head is off-frame until about f189, so it briefly looks like two eels.
- f264-f267 is nearly black for about 0.2 s.
Depends on caption: following the path does not. Knowing that the pucker and tunnel are the "throat", rather than just a hole and a tube, does.
naive.q3:
Partly, and only after a beat.
Inside (f315-f378): the tip threads between red comb-like arches toward a bright crescent opening with water and plants beyond. That clearly reads as "a way out to the open water", but a first-time viewer will not know the arches are gills. They read as ribs or combs, so "a gap in the gills" depends on the caption.
Outside (f381): it cuts to a tight shot of a brown surface with a dark red slit. Neither the fish's eye nor its head is in frame until about f390-f393, and the tail tip is a small blue hook (roughly 40x50 px on a 1080-wide frame, about 4% of width) at the top of the slit, plus one bubble. On a phone the first ~0.3 s is "what am I looking at?". It resolves as the camera pulls back (f396-f429) and the eye appears. From then on the exit point is clear without words: the top of the gill slit, just behind the eye, on the side of the head (wide shot f417-f477).
One snag: the tail then lies backward along the upper flank, which does not match the frame-one pose of hanging down over the pectoral fin. If you remember the hook, the geometry doesn't add up.
Depends on caption: the location is readable from the pictures; the anatomy name ("gills") needs the caption.
naive.q4:
Only just, and the timing is off.
On the cut at f479 (16.0 s) a head with an eye suddenly appears at the gill slit, tucked under the edge of the gill cover. It then sits essentially still for about 4.7 s (f479-f618) while the body loops. From the pictures alone it looks as if the head is already out: the eye is on the outside and visible throughout. So no "head comes out" event happens at the narration line (caption "Its HEAD comes out LAST" runs f480-f537), and with captions the line points at a head that isn't moving.
The actual release is f627-f636: the head lifts off the slit, and at f636 the slit is empty below it. That is about 0.3 s, under the caption "gives one final pull", and it cuts away to the wide shot only 3 frames later at f639.
It also happens low in the frame. The head is at roughly y 1420-1500 of 1920 (74-78%), right at the top of the Shorts title overlay band, with the slit itself inside the band, while the top ~55% of the frame is empty water. The right side of the loop also runs under the action-button column.
A viewer can catch it as "the eel snaps free" if they're looking, but it's brief and low, and it doesn't line up with the "head last" line.
Depends on caption: yes. Without one, you see a head peeking out early and then a sudden snap. With one, the caption names the beat 4.5 s before it happens.
needsCaption: f000-f047: that the blue strap is an EEL (could be a worm, parasite or sea snake) and that the fish swallowed it. The picture alone only says 'tail end of something long'.
f081-f114: that the grey strand slurped into the desaturated mouth is the same blue eel. It is grey, has no head showing and is a different colour from the hook.
f117-f171: 'Scientists filmed it on X-ray'. The scanner sweep reads as an X-ray scan, but 'scientists' and 'real footage' only come from the caption.
f270-f309: that the ribbed pink tunnel is the fish's throat.
f312-f378: that the red comb-like arches are gills ('slips through a gap in the gills'). Without the caption they read as ribs or combs.
f480-f537: 'Its head comes out last'. There is no visual event at this line; the head has been visible and still at the slit since the cut at f479, so the beat exists only in the caption.
f624-f636: 'final pull'. The snap is visible but lasts about 0.3 s; the caption is what tells you the head just came free.

findings.frames: f479-f618 (head visible and still), f627-f636 (real release), f639 (cut)
findings.claim: The 'head comes out last' beat has no visible event. The head with its eye appears at the slit on the cut at f479 and stays put for about 4.7 s, so from the pictures it looks already out. The real release happens 4.5 s later under 'final pull', lasts about 0.3 s and is cut away from 3 frames later.
findings.fix: Keep the head hidden under the gill cover (no eye showing) until the release, and stage the release during or right after 'Its head comes out last' (around f500-f540), or move the line to the release. Hold 0.5-1 s on the freed head before the f639 cut.

findings.claim: The tail's tapering tip, the cue that makes it read as a tail and not just a blue strap, ends at roughly x 900-960, y 1550-1870 of 1920. That is inside the Shorts bottom title band and against the right action-button column, so on a phone the defining taper is likely covered.
findings.fix: Reframe or scale the hook so the whole tail, including the tip, sits above about y 1450 and left of about x 880, for example by pushing the fish up and left or shortening the hanging length.

findings.claim: The climax is composed in the bottom quarter. The head and slit sit at about 72-80% of frame height, inside or touching the Shorts title band, and the right side of the loop runs under the action-button column, while the top ~55% of the frame is empty water.
findings.fix: Raise the camera or shift the frame so the slit and head sit around 45-60% height, and keep the loop left of about x 880.

findings.frames: f540-f546 (tail tip around (350,1370) next to eye at (415,1380) in f543)
findings.claim: Right after the cut, the thin tail end swings round and lands beside the head at the gill slit. For a moment both ends are at the slit, which raises 'which end is which, is the tail going back in?'.
findings.fix: Route the tail's sweep below or away from the slit (keep the tip at least ~150 px from the head), or start the curl shot with the tail already rising.

findings.claim: Continuity jump on the cut: the body goes from lying straight along the flank, tail just entering at the bottom, to a big loop arching above the fish's back.
findings.fix: Bridge it with a few frames of the body lifting off the flank before the cut, or cut on a matching pose.

findings.claim: The exit shot opens on an unidentifiable brown surface with no eye or head in frame, and the emerging tip is tiny (about 40x50 px on 1080) and low-contrast blue on brown. On a phone the first ~0.3 s reads as 'what am I looking at?'.
findings.fix: Open with the fish's eye in frame (start the pull-back wider), and make the tip larger or brighter with a bigger bubble puff so the eye goes straight to it.

findings.claim: The hook pose (tail hanging down from the slit over the pectoral fin) never happens in the story. In the story the tail leaves the top of the slit and lies backward along the upper flank, so the hook image and the escape geometry don't match.
findings.fix: Either let the emerging tail droop down over the pectoral fin in S7-S8, or rebuild the hook from an actual story pose (around f450-f477, framed for the hook).

findings.claim: The swallowed strand is grey with no head showing, so nothing visually links it to the blue eel. The extreme close-up with a giant eye at the top of frame (f081-f087) briefly reads as a different creature.
findings.fix: Keep a hint of the eel's blue in the desaturated grade (or tint only the eel), and start slightly wider so the fish's head reads before the mouth fills the frame.

findings.claim: During the dissolve the ghost X-ray eel (head around (700,1440)) and the coloured eel (coil at the right edge, head off-frame until about f189) don't line up, so for a moment there seem to be two eels.
findings.fix: Line up the coloured eel's position and pose with the X-ray eel through the dissolve, or keep the coloured head in frame from f174.

findings.claim: The gill arches read as red ribs or combs. 'Gills' only comes from the caption, and the tip creeps slowly for about 2.2 s with little change.
findings.fix: Show a hint of gill flaps opening and closing with the light, or tighten the shot by about 0.5 s.

findings.frames: f447, f462 (kink at about (310-380, 1080-1130)); f480 inner-bend notch
findings.claim: Where the eel bends into the slit, its outline breaks into a small sharp arrowhead or notch, like a folded flap. At phone size it can read as an extra fin or the tail tip.
findings.fix: Smooth the bend geometry and outline join where the body crosses the gill cover edge.

findings.claim: The leading head of the departing eel travels into the bottom-left of the Shorts title band (about 80-86% height), so the 'swims away' face is partly covered.
findings.fix: Angle the swim path more leftward or upward so the head stays above about 75% height.

findings.claim: The hero curl shot is bottom-heavy and clipped. The eel loop touches or runs off the right frame edge for most of the shot, and the predator's eye is cut by the left edge. All the action sits in the lower ~45% of the frame, and the top ~45% is empty water. On a phone the curl reads as a cropped ring rather than a full figure.
findings.fix: Reframe S10: pull back 12-15% and pan right about 120 px, so the loop's outer rim stays at least 60 px inside the right edge and the eye clears the left edge. Then tilt up so the eel occupies roughly y 650-1500 of 1920. That frees space and still keeps the top caption band (y<520) clear.

findings.shot: S10 end into cut to S11
findings.claim: The 'beat on the freed head' isn't a beat. Frame-to-frame motion peaks here (mean diff 8-12, against 2-7 earlier in the shot). The camera pushes and tilts while the tail whips about 850 px across the frame in 4 frames (f633-f637), threading through the loop. At f638 the head is half out of frame left just before the cut. The payoff gets scrambled.
findings.fix: Ease the camera to a stop by about f626 and hold. Move the tail swing earlier (finish it by f626), or stretch it over at least 10 frames. Keep the head at least 150 px inside the left edge through f638, so f629-f638 is a near-still hold on the freed head with only a small head or body settle.

findings.claim: The X-ray to stomach transition is a 2-frame dissolve, which reads as a flash frame or glitch, not a deliberate cut. The eel also jumps position: the X-ray head and coil sit centre-left, while in the stomach the coil is pinned to the right edge.
findings.fix: Either make it a clean hard cut at f174, or stretch it to an 8-12 frame dissolve (about f167-f178). Offset the S4 start framing so the stomach coil lands near where the X-ray coil was, giving a match-dissolve.

findings.claim: For the first ~0.55 s of the stomach shot, the eel's coil and head are off the right edge. Only the thin tail and a sliver of ring show while 'Inside the fish's STOMACH' plays, so the eel reads as a worm fragment until the pan catches up around f192.
findings.fix: Start the S4 camera about 250 px further right (or the eel about 250 px left), so the full coil and the head with its eye are in frame from f174. Then let the pan and push continue from there.

findings.claim: This is a jump cut: the angle is the same, the scale changes by about 0.75x, and both sides are near-static (diff ~0.3). The tail also fails to match: at f415 it is a tall hook rising from the slit and arcing toward the dorsal line, and at f416 it becomes a short, low horizontal hook. The tail visibly shrinks at the cut, and the pectoral fin changes shape.
findings.fix: Match the tail pose across the cut: start S8 with the same rise angle and length, scaled to the new framing. Or replace the cut with a continuous pull-back from S7, or change the angle enough that it reads as a new shot.

findings.claim: A second, lighter, finely hatched eel band runs just above and behind the main eel body on the right half of the frame. The body reads as doubled or ghosted.
findings.fix: Hide or occlude the far body segment in S9. Either z-sort it under the near segment and clip it to the fish flank, or don't draw it until it is needed for the S10 curl.

findings.claim: The eel's contact shadow is built from overlapping hard-edged dark circles. It shows as a row of dark beads under the eel in S9 and as dark blobs inside the loop in S10, reading as extra fish spots rather than a shadow.
findings.fix: Render the shadow as one soft path, or blur the stamped circles (gaussian 12-20 px at 1080 wide). Lower its opacity about 30% so the circle edges disappear.

findings.claim: Right after the cut, the eel's U-bend has a sharp V-kink: the tail folds back at an acute angle beside the predator's pectoral fin. For about 6 frames the eel looks broken.
findings.fix: Set a minimum spine bend radius (about 40 px at 1080) for S11's opening pose, or open the first pose into a soft S-curve that straightens over f639-f650.

findings.claim: At phone size the poke-out tip is small: about 40 px at 1080 wide, roughly 14 pt on screen. It is dark blue against the dark red slit, and the camera is already pulling out. The bubbles carry most of the read for this beat.
findings.fix: Start S7 about 1.3x tighter, or hold the pull-out until about f400. Add a light rim or highlight on the tip so it separates from the slit.

findings.claim: A near-dead hold (f141-f148, diff <0.6) is followed by a crash zoom of about 4x in 18 frames (f150-f168), the fastest camera move in the piece. The X-ray eel jumps from small to full frame. Readable, but jarring on a phone.
findings.fix: Start the push around f136 and spread it over about 30 frames with an ease-in and ease-out, ending around f168. That removes both the hold and the snap.

findings.claim: There are about 1.5 s of near-freeze with only a slow camera push (diffs 1.2-3.7). The head sits motionless in the slit, so the beat reads as paused rather than straining.
findings.fix: Add a slow body slide (move the highlight or texture along the eel toward the right), plus a small head shift or eye blink about every 12-15 frames. The beat then reads as the eel working itself out.

verified.claim: In the first beat after the cut the eel's tail is folded into a hard-cornered hairpin with a visible crease line at the fold: a V-fold at f639-641, an L-shape at f643, an acute fold at f645 and a hooked tip at f647. minors.claim: The tail end is a blunt, squared-off cap: a flat end with a corner, bent right and down. It is not the tapered, pointed eel tail seen in S6 and in the later arch. It also changes from dark navy with a pale rim (S6) to light slate-blue with a dark outline (S7) across the match cut.
minors.fix: Use the same tapered tail tip and a similar colour and rim treatment on both sides of the f380/f381 match cut.

minors.claim: As the tail tip slides up past the caught head, it is drawn frayed and soft-faded where it crosses the gill-cover edge, like 3-4 separate strands or a broom (f544-546). It then covers the eel's eye (fully at f548-549), so for about 0.15 s there are two prongs at the slit and no eye.
minors.fix: Route the tail tip around the head (outside or behind it) instead of across the front of the eye, and mask the tip against the cover with a hard edge instead of a feathered fade.

minors.claim: Where the eel's snout and neck cross the gill-cover edge as the head starts to slide out, the eel is faded with a soft brownish gradient instead of being cleanly hidden. At phone size this shows as a small pointed beak or hook on the snout (f617-619).
minors.fix: Use a hard occlusion mask at the cover edge (or a cover lip drawn on top) for these frames.

minors.claim: Large soft white bokeh discs (about 100 px full-res, about 30 px on phone) pop in for 1-2 frames and jump position. At f684 one sits right next to the eel, and at f708 one crosses the eel's body. They read as flickering smudges or ghosts, not drifting particles.
minors.fix: Slow the near-camera motes so each one drifts across over many frames, cap their size or opacity, or drop the biggest ones and keep them off the eel's path.

minors.frames: f540-f546 (tail tip around (350,1370) next to eye at (415,1380) in f543)
minors.claim: Right after the cut, the thin tail end swings round and lands beside the head at the gill slit. For a moment both ends are at the slit, which raises 'which end is which, is the tail going back in?'.
minors.fix: Route the tail's sweep below or away from the slit (keep the tip at least ~150 px from the head), or start the curl shot with the tail already rising.

minors.claim: Continuity jump on the cut: the body goes from lying straight along the flank, tail just entering at the bottom, to a big loop arching above the fish's back.
minors.fix: Bridge it with a few frames of the body lifting off the flank before the cut, or cut on a matching pose.

minors.claim: The exit shot opens on an unidentifiable brown surface with no eye or head in frame, and the emerging tip is tiny (about 40x50 px on 1080) and low-contrast blue on brown. On a phone the first ~0.3 s reads as 'what am I looking at?'.
minors.fix: Open with the fish's eye in frame (start the pull-back wider), and make the tip larger or brighter with a bigger bubble puff so the eye goes straight to it.

minors.claim: The hook pose (tail hanging down from the slit over the pectoral fin) never happens in the story. In the story the tail leaves the top of the slit and lies backward along the upper flank, so the hook image and the escape geometry don't match.
minors.fix: Either let the emerging tail droop down over the pectoral fin in S7-S8, or rebuild the hook from an actual story pose (around f450-f477, framed for the hook).

minors.claim: The swallowed strand is grey with no head showing, so nothing visually links it to the blue eel. The extreme close-up with a giant eye at the top of frame (f081-f087) briefly reads as a different creature.
minors.fix: Keep a hint of the eel's blue in the desaturated grade (or tint only the eel), and start slightly wider so the fish's head reads before the mouth fills the frame.

minors.claim: During the dissolve the ghost X-ray eel (head around (700,1440)) and the coloured eel (coil at the right edge, head off-frame until about f189) don't line up, so for a moment there seem to be two eels.
minors.fix: Line up the coloured eel's position and pose with the X-ray eel through the dissolve, or keep the coloured head in frame from f174.

minors.claim: The gill arches read as red ribs or combs. 'Gills' only comes from the caption, and the tip creeps slowly for about 2.2 s with little change.
minors.fix: Show a hint of gill flaps opening and closing with the light, or tighten the shot by about 0.5 s.

minors.frames: f447, f462 (kink at about (310-380, 1080-1130)); f480 inner-bend notch
minors.claim: Where the eel bends into the slit, its outline breaks into a small sharp arrowhead or notch, like a folded flap. At phone size it can read as an extra fin or the tail tip.
minors.fix: Smooth the bend geometry and outline join where the body crosses the gill cover edge.

minors.claim: The leading head of the departing eel travels into the bottom-left of the Shorts title band (about 80-86% height), so the 'swims away' face is partly covered.
minors.fix: Angle the swim path more leftward or upward so the head stays above about 75% height.

minors.claim: The X-ray to stomach transition is a 2-frame dissolve, which reads as a flash frame or glitch, not a deliberate cut. The eel also jumps position: the X-ray head and coil sit centre-left, while in the stomach the coil is pinned to the right edge.
minors.fix: Either make it a clean hard cut at f174, or stretch it to an 8-12 frame dissolve (about f167-f178). Offset the S4 start framing so the stomach coil lands near where the X-ray coil was, giving a match-dissolve.

minors.claim: For the first ~0.55 s of the stomach shot, the eel's coil and head are off the right edge. Only the thin tail and a sliver of ring show while 'Inside the fish's STOMACH' plays, so the eel reads as a worm fragment until the pan catches up around f192.
minors.fix: Start the S4 camera about 250 px further right (or the eel about 250 px left), so the full coil and the head with its eye are in frame from f174. Then let the pan and push continue from there.

minors.claim: This is a jump cut: the angle is the same, the scale changes by about 0.75x, and both sides are near-static (diff ~0.3). The tail also fails to match: at f415 it is a tall hook rising from the slit and arcing toward the dorsal line, and at f416 it becomes a short, low horizontal hook. The tail visibly shrinks at the cut, and the pectoral fin changes shape.
minors.fix: Match the tail pose across the cut: start S8 with the same rise angle and length, scaled to the new framing. Or replace the cut with a continuous pull-back from S7, or change the angle enough that it reads as a new shot.

minors.claim: A second, lighter, finely hatched eel band runs just above and behind the main eel body on the right half of the frame. The body reads as doubled or ghosted.
minors.fix: Hide or occlude the far body segment in S9. Either z-sort it under the near segment and clip it to the fish flank, or don't draw it until it is needed for the S10 curl.

minors.claim: The eel's contact shadow is built from overlapping hard-edged dark circles. It shows as a row of dark beads under the eel in S9 and as dark blobs inside the loop in S10, reading as extra fish spots rather than a shadow.
minors.fix: Render the shadow as one soft path, or blur the stamped circles (gaussian 12-20 px at 1080 wide). Lower its opacity about 30% so the circle edges disappear.

minors.claim: Right after the cut, the eel's U-bend has a sharp V-kink: the tail folds back at an acute angle beside the predator's pectoral fin. For about 6 frames the eel looks broken.
minors.fix: Set a minimum spine bend radius (about 40 px at 1080) for S11's opening pose, or open the first pose into a soft S-curve that straightens over f639-f650.

minors.claim: At phone size the poke-out tip is small: about 40 px at 1080 wide, roughly 14 pt on screen. It is dark blue against the dark red slit, and the camera is already pulling out. The bubbles carry most of the read for this beat.
minors.fix: Start S7 about 1.3x tighter, or hold the pull-out until about f400. Add a light rim or highlight on the tip so it separates from the slit.

minors.claim: A near-dead hold (f141-f148, diff <0.6) is followed by a crash zoom of about 4x in 18 frames (f150-f168), the fastest camera move in the piece. The X-ray eel jumps from small to full frame. Readable, but jarring on a phone.
minors.fix: Start the push around f136 and spread it over about 30 frames with an ease-in and ease-out, ending around f168. That removes both the hold and the snap.

minors.claim: There are about 1.5 s of near-freeze with only a slow camera push (diffs 1.2-3.7). The head sits motionless in the slit, so the beat reads as paused rather than straining.
minors.fix: Add a slow body slide (move the highlight or texture along the eel toward the right), plus a small head shift or eye blink about every 12-15 frames. The beat then reads as the eel working itself out.
